title: Thermal In Motion: Designing Thermal Flow Illusions with Tactile and Thermal Interaction
authors: Singhal, Yatharth; Honrales, Daniel; Wang, Haokun; Kim, Jin Ryong
thermalVocabularyDescription: thermal motion, flowing thermal sensation, thermal referral, warm, cool, hot, cold
emotionAffectMeasurement: No direct emotion scale; focused on thermal motion perception and interviews.
thermalAffectJustification: Primarily empirical, focused on immersion rather than formal affect theory.
thermalCuePurpose: Create a perceived moving thermal cue for more immersive VR interaction.
mainActuatorPossibleTemperatureRange: Relative -15C to +9C from neutral skin temperature
temporalParameters: Warm-up around 1-3s, motion durations up to 10s
technicalSummary: Peltier and vibration were combined to produce a thermal motion illusion.
studyMethods: Multiple psychophysical user studies and qualitative interviews
contributions: Introduces thermal motion and key parameters for generating it.
contributionsToDesign: Shows how synchronized thermo-tactile timing can improve perceived motion and immersion.

title: Designing Beyond Hot and Cold - Exploring Full-Body Heat Experiences in Sauna
authors: Moesgen, Tim; Gowrishankar, Ramyah; Xiao, Yu
thermalVocabularyDescription: pressure, tingling, sparks, movement, discomfort
emotionTheoriesUsage: No explicit emotion model; grounded in phenomenology and somaesthetics.
thermalAffectJustification: Mainly from prior empirical HCI and lived sauna experience.
thermalCuePurpose: Understand and articulate full-body heat experience.
mainActuatorPossibleTemperatureRange: 80C to 90C environmental sauna heat
temporalParameters: Two sittings of around 10 minutes each
otherNote: No wearable thermal actuator in this paper.
technicalSummary: An observational study of naturally occurring whole-body heat experience.
studyMethods: Phenomenological interviews, body map, and sensory elicitation artifacts
contributions: Expands language and dimensions for describing heat experience.
contributionsToDesign: Proposes design parameters such as motion, timbre, and distribution.

title: Enhancing Food Coldness Perception via Synchronous Posterior Neck Cold stimulus during Swallowing
authors: Komiya, Shin'ichi; Nitto, Ryota; Ban, Yuki; Warisawa, Shin'ichi
thermalVocabularyDescription: cold stimulus, cooling sensation, coldness perception, thermal feedback
emotionAffectMeasurement: No emotion metric; comfort and deliciousness were secondary outcomes.
thermalAffectJustification: Focus on sensory perception enhancement rather than affect.
thermalCuePurpose: Enhance perceived food coldness without changing food temperature.
mainActuatorPossibleTemperatureRange: Cooling around 2.5-3.0C below baseline skin in constant condition
temporalParameters: Swallow and pre-swallow synchronization around 3s
technicalSummary: Posterior neck cooling synchronized with swallowing increased perceived coldness.
studyMethods: Within-subject experimental user study with paired comparisons
contributions: Demonstrates temporal synchronization as a critical parameter for cross-modal coldness enhancement.
contributionsToDesign: Provides timing guidance for thermal-food interaction design.

title: Thermal Masking: When the Illusion Takes Over the Real
authors: Wang, Haokun; Singhal, Yatharth; Gil, Hyunjae; Kim, Jin Ryong
thermalVocabularyDescription: thermal masking, thermal referral, thermal migration, thermal illusion
thermalCuePurpose: Investigate thermal masking and perceptual relocation of thermal sensation.
mainActuatorPossibleTemperatureRange: -8C to +6C relative to skin temperature
temporalParameters: Thermal around 5s, vibrotactile around 7s
technicalSummary: Shows vibrotactile cues can mask and relocate perceived thermal sensation.
studyMethods: Three controlled user studies with repeated-measures psychophysical methods
contributions: Introduces thermal masking effects and engineering implications for thermal displays.
contributionsToDesign: Supports designing larger perceived thermal coverage with fewer thermal actuators.

title: Hydroptical Thermal Feedback: Spatial Thermal Feedback Using Visible Lights and Water
authors: Ichihashi, Sosuke; Inami, Masahiko; Ho, Hsin-Ni; Howell, Noura
thermalVocabularyDescription: hydroptical thermal feedback, apparent motion, perceived water temperature
thermalCuePurpose: Create spatial and moving thermal sensations in water without changing bulk water temperature.
mainActuatorPossibleTemperatureRange: Perceived around 28C to 38C depending on illuminance
temporalParameters: Stimulus durations around 1-5s and SOA around 200-1000ms
technicalSummary: Visible light in water produced local warming, thermal apparent motion, and temperature illusion.
studyMethods: Four psychophysical studies
contributions: Introduces hydroptical thermal feedback as a new interaction method.
contributionsToDesign: Provides design recommendations and trade-offs for light-water thermal interaction.

title: Augmented Breathing via Thermal Feedback in the Nose
authors: Brooks, Jas; Mazursky, Alex; Hixon, Janice; Lopes, Pedro
thermalCuePurpose: Alter perceived airflow and breathing ease via synchronized intranasal heating/cooling.
mainActuatorPossibleTemperatureRange: Offsets around -10.5C to +10.6C from baseline intranasal temperature
temporalParameters: Synchronized to inhalation duration around 1.81s
technicalSummary: Intranasal thermal stimulation changed perceived breathing resistance without mechanical obstruction.
studyMethods: Psychophysical staircase and qualitative study
contributions: Demonstrates bidirectional perceived airflow modulation from thermal cues.
contributionsToDesign: Suggests thermal breathing feedback for VR, meditation, and assistive interactions.

title: ALCool: Utilizing Alcohol's Evaporative Cooling for Ubiquitous Cold Sensation Feedback
authors: Hamazaki, Takumi; Takami, Taiki; Ushiyama, Keigo; Mizoguchi, Izumi; Kajimoto, Hiroyuki
thermalCuePurpose: Provide low-power, long-duration cold sensation via alcohol evaporation and airflow.
mainActuatorPossibleTemperatureRange: Cooling intensity depends on evaporation and fan speed
temporalParameters: 30s stimulation windows, effective cooling up to around 30-60 min per refill
technicalSummary: A wearable cooling system using alcohol evaporation achieved cold sensation with low power.
studyMethods: Two user studies plus technical evaluation
contributions: Presents a practical low-power alternative to Peltier-heavy cooling wearables.
contributionsToDesign: Supports ubiquitous cooling feedback and combined thermal-olfactory interaction design.
powerEnergyConsumption: Low power relative to Peltier baseline in the paper

title: Trigeminal-based Temperature Illusions
authors: Brooks, Jas; Nagels, Steven; Lopes, Pedro
thermalCuePurpose: Create warm/cool illusions via trigeminal scent stimulation without changing physical temperature.
mainActuatorModel: Piezo micro-pumps with vibrating mesh atomizer
mainActuatorPossibleTemperatureRange: Perceptual illusion, not direct temperature control
temporalParameters: Around 1s atomization with roughly 6-12s intervals
technicalSummary: Demonstrates temperature illusion in VR through trigeminal stimulation.
studyMethods: Two controlled studies (pairwise ratings and VR evaluation)
contributions: Introduces a low-power non-Peltier route for perceived thermal feedback.
contributionsToDesign: Shows trigeminal thermal illusion can shape perceived environmental temperature in VR.

title: The Impact of Thermal Cues on Affective Responses to Emotionally Resonant Vibrations
authors: Macdonald, Shaun Alexander; Pollick, Frank; Brewster, Stephen Anthony
emotionTheoriesUsage: Used as the analysis frame for valence and arousal responses.
emotionAffectMeasurement: Likert self-reports for valence, arousal, and emotional resonance.
thermalAffectJustification: Builds on prior thermotactile affect literature.
thermalCuePurpose: Test how thermal congruence modulates affective response to vibrotactile patterns.
mainActuatorPossibleTemperatureRange: 24C cold, 30C neutral, 34-36C warm
technicalSummary: Combines thermal and vibrotactile cues to examine affective resonance changes.
studyMethods: Controlled within-subject lab experiment
contributions: Reports how thermal context shifts perceived emotional qualities of vibration.
contributionsToDesign: Guides thermo-vibrotactile composition for emotional interaction design.

title: Therminator: Understanding the Interdependency of Visual and On-Body Thermal Feedback in Virtual Reality
authors: Gunther, Sebastian; Muller, Florian; Schon, Dominik; Elmoghazy, Omar; Muhlhauser, Max; Schmitz, Martin
thermalCuePurpose: Study visual-thermal interdependency and perceived temperature realism in VR.
mainActuatorForTemperatureSensation: Water flow through PE-RT tube network
mainActuatorPossibleTemperatureRange: About 18C to 48C system range; tested 22.5C to 42.5C
temporalParameters: About 25s stimulation with around 12s full cold-to-hot transition capability
technicalSummary: A liquid-based on-body thermal display integrated with VR visuals.
studyMethods: Controlled within-subject VR experiment
contributions: Shows how visual context and thermal feedback jointly shape perception and comfort.
contributionsToDesign: Provides practical congruence guidance for thermal VR design.

title: Coldness Presentation to Ventral Forearm using Electrical Stimulation with Elastic Gel and Anesthetic Cream
authors: Saito, Taiga; Hamazaki, Takumi; Kaneko, Seitaro; Kajimoto, Hiroyuki
thermalVocabularyDescription: cold, coldness, cold sensation, electrical stimulation, thermal nociceptors
thermalCuePurpose: Present cold-like sensations on the forearm via current-controlled electrical stimulation with pain-suppression schemes.
mainActuatorPossibleTemperatureRange: Not true temperature feedback; current varied per participant.
temporalParameters: 2 s bursts at 100 pps; 27 Hz scan across electrodes.
otherNote: Ambient temperature not reported; not temperature-based stimulation.
technicalSummary: Electrical stimulation through gel or anesthetic cream explores stable cold-sensation presentation on the ventral forearm.
studyMethods: Within-subjects lab study (gel vs cream), 12 participants, 732 trials per participant.
contributions: Maps cold reports across pulse width, polarity, and electrode location; compares pain-suppression methods.
contributionsToDesign: Documents limitations and prevalence of electrically evoked cold sensations for VR thermal metaphors.

title: DexteriSync: A Hand Thermal I/O Exoskeleton for Morphing Finger Dexterity Experience
authors: Shen, Ximing; Kamiyama, Youichi; Minamizawa, Kouta; Nishida, Jun
thermalVocabularyDescription: thermal, cold, warm, hot, thermal grill, dexterity, skin temperature
thermalCuePurpose: Morph finger dexterity and thermal perception via liquid-cooled/heated copper tubes on thumb and index.
mainActuatorForTemperatureSensation: Water circulation in copper and silicone tubes with Peltier-cooled reservoir
mainActuatorModel: PID water temperature; 5°C and 40°C water conditions
mainActuatorPossibleTemperatureRange: Room 25±1°C; cold water 5±1.5°C; warm 40±1.5°C; skin temps reported for thumb and index.
temporalParameters: 10–15 min for stabilised skin temperature; study blocks up to ~90 min.
technicalSummary: Wearable exoskeleton circulates temperature-controlled water to dorsal thumb and index for dexterity and thermal-perception studies.
studyMethods: Technical evaluation, pegboard dexterity study, JND-style temperature matching, design workshop.
contributions: Demonstrates thermal-motor coupling and thermal-grill-style imbalance on two fingers.
contributionsToDesign: Example parameters for cold exposure duration and finger placement for embodied design probes.

title: Smiles Summon the Warmth of Spring: A Design Framework for Thermal-Affective Interaction based in Chinese Cí Poetry
authors: Feng, Feng; Bennett, Dan; Mekler, Elisa D.
emotionTheoriesUsage: Lexical analysis of poetry; affect theories cited but not used as primary mapping model.
emotionAffectMeasurement: No empirical affect measures; conceptual framework from text.
thermalCuePurpose: Derive experiential vocabulary and design concepts for thermal-affective HCI from classical Chinese poetry.
otherNote: No wearable prototype; multisensory in concepts only.
technicalSummary: Framework of experiential qualities, multisensory factors, and thermal-affect interaction directions.
studyMethods: Grounded theory on poetry; three design case analyses.
contributions: Seven vocabulary patterns; argues against simple universal temperature-to-emotion mappings.
contributionsToDesign: Scaffolds richer articulation of thermal experience for designers.

title: ThermoGrasp: Enabling Localized Thermal Feedback on Fingers for Precision Grasps in Virtual Reality
authors: Nasser, Arshad; Hasan, Khalad
thermalVocabularyDescription: hot, cold as warming/cooling rate cues; thermal grasp icon
thermalCuePurpose: Localised fingertip Peltier feedback aligned with VR grasp patterns.
mainActuatorPossibleTemperatureRange: ±3°C/s change rate; 3.5 s on-time per trial.
powerConsumption: Up to 400 mA at 6 V per module
temporalParameters: 3.5 s stimulus; ~1.5 s to ~5.25°C delta.
technicalSummary: Five thin Peltiers on fingertips with selective activation by grasp cardinality; two VR user studies.
studyMethods: Study 1: 12 participants, TGI recognition; Study 2: 12 participants, HX questionnaire in VR.
contributions: Reports recognition accuracy and preferred feedback mapping for VR grasps.
contributionsToDesign: Shows exact vs extra-finger thermal feedback trade-offs for VR objects.
powerEnergyConsumption: Up to ~12 W if all five modules active.

title: Flip-Pelt: Motor-Driven Peltier Elements for Rapid Thermal Stimulation and Congruent Pressure Feedback in Virtual Reality
authors: Kang, Seongjun; Kim, Gwangbin; Hwang, Seokhyun; Park, Jeongju; Elsharkawy, Ahmed Ibrahim Ahmed Mohamed; Kim, SeungJun
thermalVocabularyDescription: warm, cool, hot, cold, rapid thermal stimulation, pressure congruence
thermalCuePurpose: Flip pre-heated or pre-cooled Peltier sides against skin for fast thermal cues plus pressure in VR.
mainActuatorModel: Dual-sided Peltier with silicone barrier; ~2.0 V, 0.6 A per element
mainActuatorPossibleTemperatureRange: Warm side capped at 40°C; cool side ~16–28°C at 2.0 V per paper.
temporalParameters: Study 1: 3 s stimulus, ≥10 s rest; Study 2: 20 s segments.
technicalSummary: Eight motorised flippable Peltiers deliver paired thermal and pressure cues; VR demos and recognition study.
studyMethods: Study 1: 14 participants pattern recognition; Study 2: 14 participants HX ratings in two VR scenarios.
contributions: Demonstrates sub-second motor flip vs slower conventional Peltier ramping.
contributionsToDesign: Spatial thermal-pressure patterns for material stiffness illusion.
powerEnergyConsumption: ~9.6 W eight elements; ~51 min on 3.7 V 2200 mAh pack (paper estimate).

title: Assessing the Influence of Visual Cues in Virtual Reality on the Spatial Perception of Physical Thermal Stimuli
authors: Gunther, Sebastian; Skogseide, Alexandra; Buhlmann, Robin; Mühlhäuser, Max
thermalVocabularyDescription: warm, heat, thermal feedback, thermal perception, spatial localisation
thermalCuePurpose: Measure how VR visual heat-source location affects perceived location of eight on-body Peltiers.
mainActuatorPossibleTemperatureRange: Heating at 3°C/s to 40°C; 10 s actuation.
temporalParameters: 10 s per stimulus; 3°C/s ramp.
technicalSummary: Eight spaced Peltiers on non-dominant arm and hand with matched/mismatched VR visuals.
studyMethods: 20 participants; 9×9 thermal×visual location factorial; ART non-parametric analysis.
contributions: Reports low localisation accuracy except hand; tolerance bands in cm per segment.
contributionsToDesign: Suggests fewer actuators may suffice given visual dominance and spatial blur.

title: Non-Contact Thermal Haptics for VR
authors: Wang, Yida; Chen, Yi-Chao
thermalVocabularyDescription: thermal haptics, heated air, non-contact, thermal display
thermalCuePurpose: Direct heated air with ultrasonic beam steering for contactless VR thermal feedback.
mainActuatorForTemperatureSensation: Resistive heaters plus 40 kHz ultrasonic array
mainActuatorPossibleTemperatureRange: Heating circuit limited at 40°C; 2.5 W heater power.
otherNote: No empirical thermal perception measures reported.
technicalSummary: Prototype combines resistive warming and phased-array airflow; no user perception study in paper.
studyMethods: System description only; future work notes user studies.
contributions: Architecture for spatial 'thermal pixels' over ~60 cm grid at 1 m.
contributionsToDesign: Non-contact thermal pixel concept for large-area VR.

title: MCU-Based Hot Compression Belt Control System as Menstrual Cramp Reliever
authors: Borris, Darianne Mae S.; De Chavez, Mark Anthony D.; De Ocampo, Denise R.; Linsangan, Noel B.; De Leon, Voltaire B.; Villaverde, Jocelyn Flores; Juanatas, Roben A.
thermalVocabularyDescription: heat, compression, abdominal temperature, thermotherapy
thermalCuePurpose: PID-controlled abdominal heating with pneumatic compression for dysmenorrhea relief.
mainActuatorModel: Four heaters; LM35 sensors; PIC microcontroller
mainActuatorPossibleTemperatureRange: Low/mid/high heat bands; initial mean abdominal temp ~35.22°C cited.
heatControlMethod: PID (Mountain Cliff algorithm) three heat levels
temporalParameters: 3 min heating in experiments; user-configurable timer.
technicalSummary: Belt prototype combining heat and compression; small-N pain before/after study.
studyMethods: 15 female participants across age brackets; pain tool before/after.
contributions: Reports pain-rate reduction correlation with heating sessions.
contributionsToDesign: Example timer-based heating and compression parameters for wearables.

title: Too Hot to Handle: An Evaluation of the Effect of Thermal Visual Representation on User Grasping Interaction in Virtual Reality
authors: Blaga, Andreea Dalia; Frutos-Pascual, Maite; Creed, Chris; Williams, Ian
thermalVocabularyDescription: hot, cold, steam, ice, thermal visual cues
thermalCuePurpose: Study how purely visual hot/cold mug contents change VR grasp aperture, location, and type.
technicalSummary: Leap Motion captures grasps on virtual mugs with hot, cold, or empty visuals under four environment styles.
studyMethods: 50 participants; 24 within-subject conditions; Friedman analysis.
contributions: Shows visual thermal cues alone shift grasp behaviour and presence.
contributionsToDesign: Recommends handle placement for visually 'hot' virtual containers.

title: Let It Snow: Designing Snowfall Experience in VR
authors: Wang, Haokun; Singhal, Yatharth; Kim, Jin Ryong
thermalVocabularyDescription: cold, snow, rain, thermo-tactile, Peltier, ultrasound
thermalCuePurpose: Combine cold airflow from Peltier packs with mid-air ultrasound tactility for snow/rain VR.
mainActuatorForTemperatureSensation: Six Peltier packs with water cooling and fans
mainActuatorPossibleTemperatureRange: Hand area cooled toward 10°C from 22°C in ~100 s; study temps 22, 15.5, 9.5°C.
temporalParameters: 1.5 s and 3 s tactile motifs; 10 s threshold trials; 30 s UX blocks.
technicalSummary: Hex chamber cold air plus ultrasound patterns for flake melt vs rain splash.
studyMethods: Three evaluations: identification, staircase mismatch thresholds, UX scales.
contributions: Thresholds for visuo-haptic precipitation density and modality preferences.
contributionsToDesign: Joint cold-air and ultrasound timing/diameter parameters for weather VR.
powerEnergyConsumption: Reports ~2600 W peak budget including many Peltier plates (lab bench).

title: The Effects of Avatar and Environment on Thermal Perception and Skin Temperature in Virtual Reality
authors: Kocur, Martin; Jackermeier, Lukas; Schwind, Valentin; Henze, Niels
thermalVocabularyDescription: fire, ice, thermal sensation, thermal comfort, skin temperature
thermalCuePurpose: Measure subjective thermal sensation and hand skin temperature under fire vs ice avatars and worlds.
technicalSummary: 4-condition within-subject game; continuous thermocouples; Lee VAS and Bedford comfort scales.
studyMethods: 32 participants; 5 min blocks; skin temp at 4 Hz.
contributions: Shows visual theming shifts reported warmth/coolness and some skin temperature trends.
contributionsToDesign: Caution on inferring physical heat from avatar styling alone.

title: Haptic around: multiple tactile sensations for immersive environment and interaction in virtual reality
authors: Han, Ping-Hsuan; Chen, Yang-Sheng; Lee, Kong-Chang; Wang, Hao-Cheng; Hsieh, Chiao-En; Hsiao, Jui-Chun; Chou, Chien-Hsing; Hung, Yi-Ping
thermalVocabularyDescription: heat, cold, mist, wind, desert, snow mountain
thermalCuePurpose: Room-scale steerable modules for radiant heat, hot air, mist cooling, and wind with VR scenes.
mainActuatorForTemperatureSensation: Heat lamp, heat blower, mist makers, fans
mainActuatorPossibleTemperatureRange: From ~22°C room: modules shift toward ~25°C (lamp), ~38°C (blower), ~18–20°C (mist/cold stack).
temporalParameters: ~8 min per application in exploratory sessions.
technicalSummary: Hybrid ubiquitous and controller-mounted actuators; exploratory exhibition demos plus 16-participant study.
studyMethods: Within-subject 4 haptic conditions walking five VR scenes; custom Likert questionnaire.
contributions: Classification of energy-based vs flow-based heat and mist cooling approaches.
contributionsToDesign: Steerable module layout and power trade-offs for environmental VR haptics.
powerEnergyConsumption: Up to ~1683 W aggregate peak across modules (paper).

title: Making Thermostats Great Again: Investigating Touch-Based Thermal Sensation for Manual Control of Thermostats
authors: Huang, Yidong; Calvary, Gaëlle; Laurillau, Yann
thermalVocabularyDescription: warm, cold, comfort, setpoint, thermal sensation
thermalCuePurpose: Peltier touchpad reflects setpoint temperatures while users adjust a virtual thermostat.
mainActuatorPossibleTemperatureRange: Touchpad 14–26°C in 0.5°C steps; room held at 14°C.
technicalSummary: Think-aloud and behavioural logging of setpoint changes with and without thermal feedback.
studyMethods: 13 participants; two sessions; mixed qualitative and Likert items.
contributions: Shows how touch thermal cues shape exploration and comfort-range estimates.
contributionsToDesign: Touch-thermal mapping strategies for smart-home interfaces.

title: Fiery Hands: Designing Thermal Glove through Thermal and Tactile Integration for Virtual Object Manipulation
authors: Wang, Haokun; Singhal, Yatharth; Gil, Hyunjae; Kim, Jin Ryong
thermalVocabularyDescription: heat, fire, wetness illusion, thermal referral, warmth
thermalCuePurpose: Dorsal Peltiers with palmar vibrotactiles exploit thermal referral for localised VR heat.
mainActuatorPossibleTemperatureRange: +3°C over skin baseline per study; max ΔT 64°C at 2.2 V 6 A device spec.
heatControlMethod: Open/closed voltage control to steady temperature
temporalParameters: 5 s trials in lab studies; 2 s randomised bursts in fireball demo.
technicalSummary: Three user studies on placement, 52 thermal patterns, and two VR demos with interviews.
studyMethods: 16+16+10 participants across studies; drawing-based spatial reports.
contributions: Quantifies referral-based coverage on hand for complex patterns.
contributionsToDesign: Guidelines pairing dorsal heat with palmar vibration for unobstructed manipulation.
powerEnergyConsumption: Up to 13.2 W per actuator at max spec; study power not isolated.

title: Augmenting Perceived Length of Handheld Controllers: Effects of Object Handle Properties
authors: Park, Chaeyong; Choi, Seungmoon
thermalVocabularyDescription: thermal conductivity, cool, warm, passive heat flow
thermalCuePurpose: Passive aluminium vs ABS handles alter perceived length when blindfolded (no active thermal feedback).
mainActuatorPossibleTemperatureRange: Room 25°C; conductivity 0.2 vs 226 W/m·K
technicalSummary: Three experiments on softness, conductivity, and texture influencing length illusion.
studyMethods: 18 participants per experiment; repeated measures ANOVA.
contributions: Isolates thermal conductivity as a cue for perceived object scale.
contributionsToDesign: Material choice on VR controllers can bias size perception via passive cooling/warming feel.

title: An Examination of Ultrasound Mid-air Haptics for Enhanced Material and Temperature Perception in Virtual Environments
authors: Villa, Steeven; Weiss, Yannick; Hirsch, Niklas; Wiethoff, Alexander
thermalVocabularyDescription: Bedford scale labels; hue-temperature association
emotionTheoriesUsage: Explains expected colour–temperature correspondences without physical heat.
emotionAffectMeasurement: Bedford 9-point perceived temperature; congruency; IPQ; EEG MMN.
thermalCuePurpose: Test whether ultrasound mid-air haptics shifts perceived temperature with coloured objects across material states.
mainActuatorPossibleTemperatureRange: No real temperature change; room ~26°C stable within ~0.8°C.
otherNote: Thermoreceptors not directly stimulated; perceptual effect only.
technicalSummary: 30 participants; gas/liquid/solid VR objects with blue/white/red and haptics on/off.
studyMethods: Within-subject factorial; 90 trials.
contributions: Congruency gains mainly for gas/liquid renderings.
contributionsToDesign: UMH can amplify colour-driven thermal ratings without thermoelectrics.

title: Mid-Air Thermo-Tactile Feedback using Ultrasound Haptic Display
authors: Singhal, Yatharth; Wang, Haokun; Gil, Hyunjae; Kim, Jin Ryong
thermalVocabularyDescription: warm, heat pain, thermal threshold, thermo-tactile
thermalCuePurpose: Fan-forced heated air in chamber steered by ultrasound focal point for mid-air warm cues in VR.
mainActuatorPossibleTemperatureRange: Chamber up to ~54°C at 120 V tests; studies use warm detection and heat-pain thresholds.
temporalParameters: 7 s exposure per threshold trial.
technicalSummary: Exp1 staircase WDT/HPDT; Exp2 pattern ID with/without 44°C; Exp3 VR VAS immersion.
studyMethods: 12+12+16 participants across experiments.
contributions: Mean WDT ~32.8°C and HPDT ~44.6°C for this apparatus; thermo-tactile preferred in VR.
contributionsToDesign: Heater–fan–chamber tuning for stable focal warm air.

title: Somaesthetic Meditation Wearable: Exploring the Effect of Targeted Warmth Technology on Meditators' Experiences
authors: Ezer, Talia Sofia; Giron, Jonathan; Erel, Hadas; Zuckerman, Oren
thermalVocabularyDescription: warmth, soothing, grounding, hug-like heat
emotionTheoriesUsage: Frames embodied reflection on warmth during meditation.
thermalCuePurpose: On-body polyimide heater for lower abdomen/back during meditation sessions.
mainActuatorPossibleTemperatureRange: Operating band 38–42°C with current-limited 42°C cap.
temporalParameters: 10 s on / 15 s off pattern mentioned; sessions 10 min.
technicalSummary: Qualitative study with/without wearable across two 10-minute meditations.
studyMethods: 20 balanced-gender meditators; thematic analysis.
contributions: Warmth as attention anchor and distraction risk during practice.
contributionsToDesign: Timing and placement guidance for subtle thermal meditation aids.
powerEnergyConsumption: ~6.7 W peak estimate at 5 V; duty-cycled average lower.

title: Playing Cool - Winter Weather's Influence on Location-Based Gaming
authors: Back, Jon; Johansson, Karin B.
thermalVocabularyDescription: cold, freezing, gloves, batteries, snow
thermalCuePurpose: Qualitative study of family outdoor GPS game in −7°C Swedish winter.
temporalParameters: ~10 min play segments before warming breaks.
technicalSummary: Observations and interviews on endurance, dexterity, and phone battery issues in snow.
studyMethods: Field observation; group interviews; questionnaires.
contributions: Design implications for cold-climate mobile outdoor play.
contributionsToDesign: Session length, clothing, and device thermal management considerations.
powerEnergyConsumption: Phone battery discharge in cold noted.

title: Dynamic Appearance Augmentation Method that Enables Easy Prototyping of Masks for Performance
authors: Masui, Motoyasu; Takegawa, Yoshinari; Hirata, Keiji
thermalVocabularyDescription: heat, thermochromic, color change, sponge conductivity
thermalCuePurpose: Copper tape resistive heaters warm mask zones so performers feel residual heat confirming ink colour change.
mainActuatorPossibleTemperatureRange: Thermochromic range ~30–40°C; 35°C in ~7 s for tested sizes.
temporalParameters: 15 s applied voltage in tests.
technicalSummary: User study: 11 adults locate which facial zone heated without mirror.
studyMethods: Accuracy of five-zone detection; prototyping workflow.
contributions: Links sponge thickness to perceived heat for performer feedback.
contributionsToDesign: Low-cost wearable thermochromic mask pipeline.

title: ThermEarhook: Investigating Spatial Thermal Haptic Feedback on the Auricular Skin Area
authors: Nasser, Arshad; Zheng, Kexin; Zhu, Kening
thermalVocabularyDescription: hot, cold, thermal perception, auricular
thermalCuePurpose: Small Peltiers around the ear for spatial hot/cold patterns.
mainActuatorPossibleTemperatureRange: 3.5°C/s; ±5.25°C in 1.5 s at full PWM.
technicalSummary: Four studies on single-point, unilateral, bilateral, and pattern evaluation (58 participants total).
studyMethods: Within-subject accuracy and RT measures.
contributions: Shows feasible spatial resolution on auricle for future hearables.
contributionsToDesign: Layout guidance for multi-module ear-worn thermo displays.

title: ThermoCaress: A Wearable Haptic Device with Illusory Moving Thermal Stimulation
authors: Liu, Yuhu; Nishikawa, Satoshi; Seong, Young ah; Niiyama, Ryuma; Kuniyoshi, Yasuo
thermalVocabularyDescription: warm, cold, pleasantness, thermal referral, CT afferents
thermalCuePurpose: Water-pouch temperature changes plus airbag pressure create illusory moving heat/cold on forearm.
mainActuatorModel: Solenoid valves; 200 L/h pumps; three reservoir temperatures
temporalParameters: 3.75 s stimulus duration.
technicalSummary: 12 participants trace perceived motion on tablet; 90 trials factorial.
studyMethods: Within-subject 2×3 designs for two groups.
contributions: Links configuration of water channels to perceived motion and pleasantness.
contributionsToDesign: Soft wearable approach combining hydraulic thermal and pneumatic cues.

title: ThermalWear: Exploring Wearable On-chest Thermal Displays to Augment Voice Messages with Affect
authors: El Ali, Abdallah; Yang, Xingyu; Ananthanarayan, Swamy; Roeggla, Thomas; Jansen, Jack; Hartcher-O'Brien, Jess; Jansen, Kaspar; Cesar, Pablo
thermalVocabularyDescription: warm, cool, thermal display
emotionTheoriesUsage: SAM valence/arousal analysis for voice augmentation.
emotionAffectMeasurement: SAM 9-point; thermal intensity and comfort Likert scales.
thermalCuePurpose: Chest-worn Peltiers deliver warm/cool pulses timed with neutral voice messages.
mainActuatorPossibleTemperatureRange: Warm 38°C, cool 28°C vs 32°C baseline; ROC up to 1°C/s.
temporalParameters: Exp1: 7 s cues with 10 s gaps; Exp2: 4 s co-timed with audio.
technicalSummary: Two experiments on chest comfort and on emotional interpretation of spoken content.
studyMethods: 12+12 participants; 2×2×2 and 3×2 designs.
contributions: Shows thermal primes shift perceived affect of prosody-neutral speech.
contributionsToDesign: Garment integration and ROC limits for socially acceptable chest cues.

title: ThermOn: thermo-musical interface for an enhanced emotional experience
authors: Akiyama, Shimon; Sato, Katsunari; Makino, Yasutoshi; Maeno, Takashi
thermalVocabularyDescription: warm, cold, dynamic thermal stimulation
emotionAffectMeasurement: SPR in pilot; like/dislike scales in main test.
thermalCuePurpose: Peltier headphone interface couples warming/cooling trajectories to music for affective listening.
mainActuatorPossibleTemperatureRange: Baseline 34°C with ±1–3°C excursions; safe band 20–40°C.
